labels.label: Mystery
labels.definition: An investigation or unresolved puzzle drives the narrative.
include: Active investigation, clues, crime-solving
exclude: Crime merely mentioned without investigative plot
examples: A detective follows clues to identify a murderer

labels.label: Fantasy
labels.definition: Supernatural or magical rules shape the fictional world.
include: Magic, mythical beings or impossible worlds essential to plot
exclude: Metaphorical magic or ordinary speculation
examples: A mage crosses a kingdom ruled by dragons

labels.label: Science fiction
labels.definition: Speculative science or technology structures the story.
include: Space exploration, future technology or scientifically framed speculation
exclude: Any futuristic date without scientific speculation
examples: An astronaut encounters an artificial intelligence

labels.label: Romance
labels.definition: The development of a love relationship is a central plot.
include: Courtship and relationship formation drive major stakes
exclude: A peripheral romantic relationship
examples: Two rivals gradually fall in love

labels.label: Historical fiction
labels.definition: A reconstructed past period centrally shapes the story.
include: Past institutions/events shape fictional characters and conflicts
exclude: Old publication date alone
examples: A fictional family struggles during a documented revolution

labels.label: Horror
labels.definition: Fear or dread is a deliberate central effect.
include: Threatening uncanny forces or terrifying sustained experiences
exclude: Violence without an intended fear effect
examples: A haunted home gradually terrorizes its inhabitants

labels.label: Literary fiction
labels.definition: Foregrounds complex interiority, language or social interpretation.
include: Narrative treatment explicitly prioritizes literary exploration
exclude: Prestige, nationality or publication imprint alone
examples: An excerpt foregrounds layered psychological interpretation

labels.label: Thriller
labels.definition: Sustained urgent suspense drives consequential danger.
include: Escalating threat, pursuit or time-critical jeopardy
exclude: A single dangerous incident
examples: A witness is pursued before exposing a conspiracy

labels.label: Adventure
labels.definition: A sequence of risky external exploits drives the plot.
include: Exploration, daring action or survival exploits
exclude: Travel as background detail
examples: An expedition navigates dangerous uncharted terrain

labels.label: Social fiction
labels.definition: Social institutions and conditions form the central conflict.
include: Institutions, collective inequity and societal critique drive plot
exclude: Any mention of a society
examples: Tenants organize against an exploitative landlord

labels.label: Satire
labels.definition: Ridicule exposes social or institutional folly.
include: Ironic exaggeration aimed at a recognizable target
exclude: Humor without a critical target
examples: Absurd bureaucratic rules expose governmental incompetence

labels.label: Dystopia
labels.definition: An imagined oppressive social order structures the story.
include: Systemic coercive future or alternative social order
exclude: An unhappy individual in an otherwise ordinary world
examples: A surveillance state controls every citizen's choices

labels.label: Revenge
labels.definition: Retaliation for a wrong is a central concern.
include: Retaliatory motive examined over the story
exclude: A fleeting angry reaction
examples: A survivor plans retribution for a betrayal

labels.label: Growth
labels.definition: Personal maturation or change is explored.
include: Learning, identity development or sustained transformation
exclude: A protagonist merely ages
examples: A sheltered teenager learns responsibility

labels.label: Family
labels.definition: Family relationships and obligations are examined.
include: Kinship conflicts, loyalty, estrangement or intergenerational ties
exclude: Family listed only as biographical context
examples: Siblings reconcile over caring for their parent

labels.label: Loss
labels.definition: Grief or separation and its consequences are explored.
include: Bereavement, irreversible deprivation or sustained absence
exclude: A death mentioned without thematic treatment
examples: A widower learns to live with grief

labels.label: Class
labels.definition: Socioeconomic hierarchy and inequality are explored.
include: Class barriers, labor relations or wealth hierarchy
exclude: Rich/poor character descriptors alone
examples: A worker confronts entrenched class privilege

labels.label: Ethics
labels.definition: Moral choices and responsibilities are examined.
include: Competing duties and explicit moral dilemmas
exclude: A clearly good or bad character with no moral inquiry
examples: A doctor must choose between conflicting duties

labels.label: Migration
labels.definition: Displacement or migration and belonging are examined.
include: Migration experience, exile and cross-border belonging
exclude: Foreign setting or author's nationality alone
examples: A displaced family negotiates a new homeland

labels.label: Identity
labels.definition: The construction or uncertainty of identity is examined.
include: Self-definition, conflicting identities or recognition
exclude: Any character introduction
examples: A person struggles between inherited and chosen identities

labels.label: Friendship
labels.definition: Friendship and mutual trust are explored.
include: Friendship development, loyalty or rupture
exclude: Companions merely share a scene
examples: Two friends rebuild trust after a betrayal

labels.label: Power
labels.definition: Acquiring, maintaining or resisting power is examined.
include: Authority, domination or political control as a sustained concern
exclude: Any powerful character
examples: A ruler's ambition corrodes alliances

labels.label: War
labels.definition: Armed conflict and its human consequences are examined.
include: Warfare, militarization or trauma in sustained treatment
exclude: A battle as a passing adventure event
examples: Soldiers struggle with the consequences of conflict

labels.label: Memory
labels.definition: Remembering, forgetting or contested recollection is examined.
include: Memory shapes identity, relationships or interpretations
exclude: A flashback used only for exposition
examples: Conflicting recollections reshape a family's past

labels.label: Investigation plot
labels.definition: A question is pursued through discovery and inference.
include: Evidence gathering and solution-seeking organize plot
exclude: A detective role without an investigative plot
examples: Characters test clues to resolve a disappearance

labels.label: Journey plot
labels.definition: Movement through successive places structures progression.
include: A goal-oriented quest or consequential travel arc
exclude: A single commute or incidental movement
examples: Travel through successive regions advances a quest

labels.label: Multiple perspectives
labels.definition: Distinct focalizing viewpoints structure narration.
include: Repeated narration from different consciousnesses
exclude: Many characters viewed by one focalizer
examples: Chapters alternate viewpoints of three protagonists

labels.label: Nonlinear narration
labels.definition: Narrative order departs substantially from chronology.
include: Recurring time shifts or rearranged chronology
exclude: A brief explanatory memory alone
examples: Alternating past and present strands reconstruct an event

labels.label: Ensemble plot
labels.definition: Several interdependent major character arcs structure plot.
include: Multiple substantially developed arcs share narrative focus
exclude: Large background cast
examples: Several households' storylines intersect

labels.label: Frame narration
labels.definition: An enclosing story introduces or contextualizes an inner story.
include: A sustained framing situation around embedded narrative
exclude: An isolated anecdote
examples: A traveler recounts a story within another narrative

labels.label: Epistolary narration
labels.definition: Letters or documents principally deliver the narrative.
include: Correspondence, diaries or records form the main telling
exclude: A letter appears as a minor prop
examples: A story unfolds through exchanged letters

labels.label: Unreliable narration
labels.definition: Narration is demonstrably misleading or limited in a consequential way.
include: Evidence contradicts or problematizes narrator account
exclude: First person alone or presumed dishonesty
examples: A narrator's account conflicts with later documented events

labels.label: First-person narration
labels.definition: A character narrates using first-person perspective.
include: Excerpt shows sustained I/we narration
exclude: Synopsis uses I or a first-person quotation only
examples: The protagonist recounts events as 'I'

labels.label: Third-person narration
labels.definition: Narrator principally refers to characters in third person.
include: Narrative excerpt uses he/she/they or names as telling stance
exclude: Synopsis grammar alone
examples: An excerpt narrates a character's thoughts in third person

labels.label: Cyclical structure
labels.definition: The ending returns consequentially to an initial situation.
include: Explicit narrative return or repetition connecting start and end
exclude: A repeated motif without structural return
examples: The closing scene repeats the opening with changed meaning

labels.label: Open ending
labels.definition: Major narrative questions remain deliberately unresolved at the close.
include: Supplied ending material leaves central outcomes unresolved
exclude: Incomplete source material or unanswered minor detail
examples: The final scene leaves the central choice unsettled

labels.label: Detective protagonist
labels.definition: A central character acts as an investigator.
include: Professional or amateur investigator is a protagonist
exclude: Detective appears only in a supporting role
examples: A private investigator leads the story

labels.label: Student protagonist
labels.definition: A central character has an explicit student role.
include: Protagonist attends an educational institution
exclude: Youth inferred to be a student
examples: A university student narrates their campus life

labels.label: Child protagonist
labels.definition: A central character is explicitly a child.
include: Specified childhood or unambiguous child age
exclude: Short stature or youthful behavior alone
examples: An eight-year-old child leads the story

labels.label: Nonhuman protagonist
labels.definition: A central character is explicitly nonhuman.
include: Animal, robot or supernatural being is central focal character
exclude: A human likened metaphorically to an animal
examples: A sentient robot seeks its origin

labels.label: Multiple protagonists
labels.definition: Several central characters share protagonist status.
include: Explicit parallel central arcs or co-protagonists
exclude: A large cast without shared centrality
examples: Three siblings each lead an interwoven plot

labels.label: Adult protagonist
labels.definition: A central character is explicitly an adult.
include: Specified adult age or clear adult status
exclude: Employment alone if age remains unclear
examples: A forty-year-old narrator revisits their childhood

labels.label: Elderly protagonist
labels.definition: A central character is explicitly in later life.
include: Explicit old age or specified elderly age
exclude: A grandparent role alone
examples: An eighty-year-old protagonist prepares a final journey

labels.label: Outsider protagonist
labels.definition: A central character occupies explicit social outsider status.
include: Exclusion or marginal social position shapes central role
exclude: A foreign name or assumed nationality
examples: An ostracized newcomer seeks acceptance

labels.label: Artist protagonist
labels.definition: A central character practices an artistic vocation.
include: Writer, musician, performer or visual artist as central role
exclude: Art appreciated as a casual hobby
examples: A painter's creative struggle drives the narrative

labels.label: Soldier protagonist
labels.definition: A central character has an explicit military role.
include: Active or former soldier with a central narrative role
exclude: Participation in conflict as a civilian
examples: A conscript narrates their deployment

labels.label: Caregiver protagonist
labels.definition: A central character has a sustained caregiving role.
include: Caregiving obligations are explicitly central
exclude: A single helpful action
examples: A nurse cares for a chronically ill relative

labels.label: Antihero protagonist
labels.definition: A central character lacks conventional heroic virtues in a consequential way.
include: Explicit morally compromised conduct structures protagonist role
exclude: Imperfection alone or villain as a minor character
examples: A self-serving protagonist pursues success through deception

labels.label: Concise prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose uses economical phrasing.
include: Excerpt shows compact direct clauses and little elaboration
exclude: Short synopsis or brief input length
examples: An excerpt uses short direct sentences with sparse modifiers

labels.label: Lyrical prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose emphasizes rhythm and evocative imagery.
include: Excerpt contains sustained musical or poetic language
exclude: Synopsis describes the work as beautiful without prose evidence
examples: An excerpt develops rhythmic nature imagery

labels.label: Colloquial prose
labels.definition: The supplied narration uses conversational register.
include: Excerpt shows informal idiom in the narration
exclude: Dialogue alone when narratorial prose is formal
examples: Narration uses everyday contractions and casual idiom

labels.label: Experimental prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose departs markedly from conventional presentation.
include: Excerpt shows sustained syntactic, typographic or linguistic experimentation
exclude: Unusual plot alone
examples: An excerpt abandons conventional syntax for fragmented patterns

labels.label: Psychological focus
labels.definition: The supplied prose foregrounds detailed inner experience.
include: Excerpt develops mental processes and introspection
exclude: Synopsis reports emotions without prose treatment
examples: A passage closely tracks shifting contradictory thoughts

labels.label: Ornate prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose uses elaborate syntax and dense embellishment.
include: Excerpt has sustained complex clauses and rich modifiers
exclude: One decorative adjective
examples: A passage layers long clauses and luxuriant description

labels.label: Minimalist prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose withholds exposition and relies on sparse detail.
include: Excerpt shows deliberate omission and suggestive spare narration
exclude: Conciseness alone without meaningful withholding
examples: A spare exchange leaves motivations unstated

labels.label: Dialogue-driven prose
labels.definition: Conversation carries much of the supplied narrative passage.
include: Substantial excerpt develops events through spoken exchanges
exclude: A single quoted line in a synopsis
examples: A long scene progresses almost entirely through dialogue

labels.label: Stream of consciousness
labels.definition: The supplied prose follows associative thought flow.
include: Excerpt shows unfiltered shifting thought and associations
exclude: Any interior monologue with orderly exposition
examples: A passage moves associatively through sensations and memories

labels.label: Descriptive prose
labels.definition: Detailed sensory description dominates supplied narration.
include: Excerpt substantially develops observed sensory particulars
exclude: A synopsis inventories settings
examples: A passage meticulously describes a room's sights and smells

labels.label: Ironic prose
labels.definition: The supplied prose maintains a consequential ironic stance.
include: Excerpt creates discernible gaps between saying and meaning
exclude: Sarcastic character dialogue alone
examples: Narration praises a failure with clearly undermining context

labels.label: Archaic register
labels.definition: The supplied prose uses historically marked language.
include: Excerpt shows sustained obsolete diction or syntax
exclude: Historical setting alone
examples: Narration consistently uses obsolete forms of address

labels.label: Tense atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence creates sustained pressure or suspense.
include: Passages or explicit narrative description support mounting unease
exclude: A lone danger with no sustained atmosphere
examples: A pursued character anticipates imminent discovery

labels.label: Dark atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports bleak or oppressive affect.
include: Persistent dread, harshness or hopelessness
exclude: Nighttime setting alone
examples: Narration sustains an oppressive sense of despair

labels.label: Warm atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports tenderness and emotional welcome.
include: Supportive interactions or consistently comforting affect
exclude: A happy ending alone
examples: Characters care tenderly for each other through hardship

labels.label: Humorous atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports a recurring comic effect.
include: Comic situations, phrasing or explicit sustained humorous tone
exclude: One character smiles
examples: Absurd misunderstandings recur with comic narration

labels.label: Bittersweet atmosphere
labels.definition: Joy and sorrow coexist in the supplied emotional treatment.
include: Mixed tenderness, regret and qualified happiness
exclude: Any sad event alongside an unrelated happy event
examples: A reunion brings joy while exposing irrevocable loss

labels.label: Melancholic atmosphere
labels.definition: Reflective sadness or wistfulness pervades supplied material.
include: Sustained sorrow, longing or contemplation of loss
exclude: A tragic event alone
examples: A narrator wistfully recalls a lost home

labels.label: Hopeful atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports anticipation of possibility or renewal.
include: Sustained affirmative expectation amid circumstances
exclude: Success in a single incident
examples: Characters retain faith in rebuilding their lives

labels.label: Uneasy atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports pervasive uncertainty or discomfort.
include: Subtle disquiet and unsettled perception
exclude: Reader uncertainty due to missing input
examples: Ordinary surroundings repeatedly feel subtly wrong

labels.label: Wonder atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports awe or astonishment.
include: Evocative encounters with extraordinary beauty or possibility
exclude: Fantasy genre alone
examples: An explorer marvels at a vast unfamiliar world

labels.label: Tranquil atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports sustained calm and repose.
include: Quiet unhurried emotional treatment
exclude: Low action count alone
examples: A passage dwells calmly on daily garden life

labels.label: Emotionally intense atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence foregrounds strong sustained emotional charge.
include: Extended urgent emotional conflict or passion
exclude: A single exclamation
examples: A confrontation unfolds through sustained anguish and urgency

labels.label: Absurd atmosphere
labels.definition: Supplied evidence supports pervasive incongruity or irrationality.
include: Repeated inexplicable situations treated as a narrative mood
exclude: A factual inconsistency in input data
examples: Characters navigate a world of nonsensical yet ordinary rules

contradictions.reason: Sparse and elaborately embellished treatment of the same passage needs scope explanation; different passages may coexist.

semantics.quality_gate: primary labels only; requires human evaluation
